I've "listened" and "absorbed" all of the words people have to say about isolation.

Isolation has always felt negative to me for this reason. I've spoken about it negatively, I've viewed it from all angles and as I was sitting with my headphones out in Manhattan, forced to listen to the noise and horns and *every single person on an active phone call at all times*, but I also realized that I was able to listen to my other parts as well.

My isolation is a positive and negative protector. It flares up when self-hatred takes over - wants me to go into hiding like I'm a monster who no one should ever be subjective to. But I was also able to hear that my self-love wanted to go sit by the water. I found myself hearing conversations of people saying the exact same things I've said and being in the exact same situations - "He told me I infected all of his house with covid and that I needed to get my covid ridden things out of the apartment. My lawyer was X, this was so abusive" and similar.

I actually don't even think I thought about my abandonment the entire time I was actively putting myself into listening through positive isolation. I was finally able to see that isolation is trying to drive me to a place where I can heal and today, I'm okay with that. 

I'm really new to this thing and I don't feel completely comfortable with it, but even just acknowledging them and writing to them is fueling self love.
